title: Truncation and heart theorem for t-admissible condensed coefficients
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$. Assume that $R$ is regular coherent, meaning that every finitely generated ideal is finitely presented and every finitely presented $R$-module has a finite resolution by finitely generated projective $R$-modules, and that $R\to\Gamma(S,\Lambda)$ is flat for every extremally disconnected profinite set $S$ (a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space in which the closure of every open set is open). These two assumptions are the meaning of t-admissibility here.

Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with Zariski locally finitely many irreducible components. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. In the ambient derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_X)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], use ordinary derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_X[0]$. Let $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(X,\Lambda)$ denote its full subcategory of dualizable objects, where dualizable means admitting evaluation and coevaluation with the two triangle identities.

The ambient standard truncation functors $\tau^{\le n}$ and $\tau^{\ge n}$ preserve $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(X,\Lambda)$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. They define the restriction of the ambient standard t-structure to this subcategory. Its heart is exactly the sheaves pro-etale locally isomorphic to
$$\Lambda_X\otimes_{\underline R}\underline N$$
for finitely presented $R$-modules $N$; the module $N$ may depend on the member of the cover. Here $\underline R$ and $\underline N$ are constant sheaves with discrete coefficients, and the tensor uses the canonical constant-section map $\underline R\to\Lambda_X$. In particular every cohomology sheaf of a dualizable object has this local form.

source.place: Definition 6.1 and Theorem 6.2(2), with Definition 3.3(1) and the notation of Section 3. This is the general t-admissible-ring theorem, not its field specialization.

proof.text: A scalar perfect complex has a bounded finite-projective representative. Coherence makes its cohomology finitely presented. The regularity hypothesis makes each such module in degree zero perfect. Set F to the isomorphism-invariant property of finitely presented modules; it contains zero. Induct on the length of a cohomological interval using the distinguished triangle truncLT(b) K -> K -> truncGE(b) K. The first term has a shorter interval; the last is the shift of its degree-b cohomology. Perfect complexes are closed under shifts and distinguished extensions. Hence bounded complexes with finitely presented cohomology are perfect, and both truncations of every scalar perfect complex are perfect. Empty intervals are zero; negative cohomological degrees and truncation bounds outside the original interval are included.

proof.text: Apply the flat ordinary scalar-realization theorem. The t-admissibility evaluation-flatness clause is exactly its hypothesis. It identifies the prescribed derived scalar realization with the termwise derived functor of ordinary scalar realization, which is additive and exact. Exact-functor comparisons therefore identify both truncations and every cohomology object of a scalar realization with the corresponding scalar realization of the truncation or ordinary realization of cohomology.

proof.text: Choose local perfect scalar models of a dualizable K on a pro-etale cover. Identified-coefficient inverse image on modules is exact, so its derived functor commutes with standard truncations. On each cover member, compose these comparisons with Step 2. Step 1 makes the resulting scalar models perfect. The reverse implication of the local-perfect-model criterion on X proves dualizability of both ambient truncations.

proof.text: Use the zero, isomorphism, shift and cone clauses of dualizable stability to make dualizableProperty an isomorphism-closed triangulated property. Mathlib ObjectProperty.HasInducedTStructure.mk' applied to Step 3 supplies its induced t-structure. The definitions of its nonpositive and nonnegative classes are exactly the ambient classes restricted to the full subcategory.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.2(2), using (3.1), Remark 3.2, (6.2), and Proposition 6.6

proof.text: For any dualizable K and integer q, take degree-q cohomology of its local scalar perfect-model isomorphisms. Exact inverse image and Step 2 give local ordinary scalar realizations of H^q(P_i). These modules are finitely presented by Step 1. The finite-presentation encoding comparison identifies the ordinary scalar realizations with precisely the finiteConstantScalarExtension models in HasScalarLocalModels. Applying this at K=M[0], q=0, and using the canonical H^0(M[0]) isomorphism gives the forward heart inclusion.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.2(2), using (3.1), Remark 3.2, (6.2), and Proposition 6.6

proof.text: Conversely convert each finite internal scalar local model of M to an ordinary finitely presented scalar module N_i by the encoding comparison. The t-admissibility regularity hypothesis makes N_i[0] perfect. Exact inverse image, Step 2, and the exact-functor single-complex comparison identify the restriction of M[0] with the prescribed derived scalar realization of N_i[0]. The local-perfect criterion gives dualizability. Together with Step 5 this proves both heart inclusions and the assertion for every cohomology sheaf; no uniform module, rank or amplitude is chosen.
